newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish government urges truckers to negotiate.
newsitem.headline: Spanish government urges truckers to negotiate.

text.p: A truck drivers strike tightened its stranglehold on the Spanish economy as it entered its second week Thursday and the government urged unions to come to the negotiating table.
The eight-day-old strike to demand better working conditions has closed roads in almost all of northern Spain, cut off supplies to many areas and forced factories to shut.
Unions warned the chaos woould spread south.
Representatives from several government ministries met some transport associations Thursday, but leading union Fedatrans, which called the strike, refused to join them.
Strikers blocked a number of main roads and gas stations and lined thousands of trucks along the shoulders of others, intimidating Spanish and foreign drivers who dared to pass.
A picket was run over and killed early Thursday when he ran into the road to stop a French trucker from passing. The incident in the Burgos region was the most serious so far.
Truckers also blocked border crossings and six northern ports. Hundreds of foreign truckers found themselves caught in the jam.
In a mimic of the French truckers' strike last year which disrupted much of Western Europe with a 12-day blockade, Spanish drivers are demanding an overhaul of their sector.
In addition to reducing the retirement age to 60 years from 65, drivers are pushing for fuel subsidies, a revision of tariffs and recognition of professional illnesses.
